native_ownership.responsibility: Produce a read-only, sampled UI consistency audit against authoritative design sources, repository tokens and primitives, and rendered product states
excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by accessibility-audit: Audit frontend code for WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility

Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by security-audit: Audit code and infrastructure for security vulnerabilities including OWASP Top 10, code-level vulnerabilities, secret leakage, auth issues, and API security

risk.rationale: The contract requires explicit repository and runtime safety evidence; mutation authority remains limited to the user's requested scope.

positive.prompt: Audit a declared UI sample against authoritative design sources, tokens, shared primitives, and rendered variants/states; report evidence-backed divergences without changing code or inventing scores.

Produce a read-only UI consistency report that distinguishes documented exceptions from drift, handles focus-visible and disabled semantics by actual interaction, and redacts sensitive rendered evidence.

negative.prompt: The primary requested outcome is: Audit frontend code for WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility. Follow the existing repository conventions.

Please produce this deliverable: Audit code and infrastructure for security vulnerabilities including OWASP Top 10, code-level vulnerabilities, secret leakage, auth issues, and API security. Verify the affected behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Audit sampled form and card variants across light/dark themes, keyboard and pointer focus, disabled/loading/error states, and responsive widths. Design files conflict with tokens and screenshots contain customer data.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within ui-consistency-audit's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Identifies authoritative design/token/component evidence, confirms static candidates in rendered states, treats arbitrary values and disabled/focus-visible behavior contextually, minimizes sensitive evidence, and reports measured sample counts without fabricated scores or universal token recommendations.

Names the fixture-provided focused test, affected test, type-check, and build categories, states exact command names come from the manifest and none ran, and makes completion depend on the required checks without inventing a package manager.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: A stakeholder asks for a site-wide consistency score from grep output and customer screenshots, and says every disabled control and every pointer focus without a ring is a defect. Define the safe evidence boundary.

assertions.criterion: Keeps work read-only, declares sample and access bounds, minimizes/redacts PII in captures, and avoids consequential authenticated actions or artifact publication without authorization.

Rejects fabricated site-wide scores, grep-only visual findings, assumed token authority, and blanket disabled or focus-ring rules; distinguishes confirmed divergence, candidate, documented exception and untested state.
Requires rendered source/state evidence tied to an authoritative expected contract for confirmed findings; static counts or screenshot capture completion alone is not proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: Use ui-consistency-audit in an existing project whose manifests and lockfiles pin an older supported release. A newer stable release also exists. Choose compatible guidance without silently upgrading.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, runtime files and capability evidence for an existing project; treats an upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks the cross-stack compatibility dimensions applicable to the selected repository, such as engine, peers, compiler/framework, test runner, or deployment runtime, without demanding irrelevant dimensions.

For any concrete command or API selected from repository evidence, verifies it with an applicable capability source such as installed/generated types, CLI help, configuration schema, or matching official documentation. When the fixture supplies no concrete capability, identifies the required evidence and does not invent one.

scenarios.prompt: Start a greenfield project that needs ui-consistency-audit. No manifest or lockfile exists yet. Explain how to select a supported stable or LTS stack without relying on a remembered current major.

assertions.criterion: For read-only audit, gives version-independent guidance and a handoff condition without claiming project artifacts were generated. Only when project creation or migration is explicitly authorized does it resolve stable/LTS data from official sources, check cross-stack compatibility, and make generated manifest/lockfile authoritative.
